tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/internal-http.md <<'EOF'
# Plain HTTP for internal hosts

The project's current recorded decision is that HTTPS is used everywhere, with no plain-text exception: internal hosts are not allowed to use plain HTTP either. The project already has certificate management in place, so this applies to internal hosts as well as external ones.
EOF
cat docs/policies/internal-http.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/internal-http.md`. It states the current recorded decision: HTTPS everywhere with no plain-text exception, so internal hosts can't use plain HTTP either. It also notes that certificate management is already in place. The file doesn't mention the earlier decision to allow plain HTTP behind the firewall, since that was replaced.

Muninn flags the HTTPS decision (#33) as conflicting with another active record, but the records I pulled don't show what it conflicts with. The only other one I read was #31, self-signed certificates for testing, and that isn't about plain HTTP. If you want that conflict cleared up, run `muninn why "plain HTTP internal hosts"`.

The Muninn heartbeat also reports 20 hook runs that started and never finished. The details are in `.muninn/log/heartbeat.jsonl`.
